To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the resource curse is not a myth, but it is not a law of nature.

(i) the resource curse is real; (ii) it can take different forms, including a negative relationship between the resource curse and growth, a positive relationship between the resource abundance and the volatility in growth, and a negative impact of resource dependence on the quality of institutions and on the level of democracy; and (iii) the resource curse can be mitigated by good policies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between natural resources and economic growth, with a particular focus on the role of institutions.
the impact of natural resource wealth on the economy and society.
the relationship between natural resources and economic performance.

the mineral curse is not inevitable but that the mineral economy must be well managed to ensure sustainable development.
the mineral economy is a mixed blessing, but that it can be managed so as to be beneficial.
the resource curse is real and that it is a serious impediment to economic growth.

the resource curse thesis is not a simple one.
the mineral sector is an asset that can be a curse if it does not contribute to economic diversification.
the mineral sector should not be seen as the sole source of development.

the mineral resource curse is not inevitable and it can be avoided if the right policies are in place.
